answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a refundable stake in an atlas of verified identities before it may transact. A sparrow-sized fake account then costs as much as a real one, so spawning thousands of sock puppets drains the attacker instead of rewarding them. Bad behaviour slashes the stake and stains the identity record, while honest work slowly raises its limit, so the nebula of cheap fake identities collapses into a small set of accountable, costly participants.
